loafo.notes: Folds are averaged within each seed; intervals are 95% Student-t intervals over seeds. AUROC_u: area under the ROC curve for unknown versus benign flows.

significance.title: Seed-Level Paired Comparison of Zero-Day Recall (Folds Averaged Within Each Seed)
significance.notes: Paired t-test over independent seeds; the six folds of one seed share a data split, so fold-level wins are not independent observations and are shown for context only.

family.title: Per-Family Zero-Day Recall and Aegis-OSR Attribution (LOAFO, α = 1%, Mean over 5 Seeds)
family.notes: The last three columns refer to Aegis-OSR. Flagged unknown: share of the withheld family labelled UNKNOWN-ATTACK or ZERO-DAY-ANOMALY. Mis-attributed: share wrongly given a known-family label. Known-family acc.: accuracy of family labels on attacks from the five known families.

temporal.title: Temporal Split by Capture Day, No Adaptation (α = 1%, Mean over 5 Seeds)
temporal.notes: Unknown-family recall of Aegis-OSR (closed-set XGB in brackets) — Thursday: WebAttack 0.998 (0.999), Infiltration 0.650 (0.000); Friday: DDoS 0.992 (0.950), PortScan 0.036 (0.027), Bot 0.009 (0.000). Recall is not comparable across rows when the realised FPR differs from the budget.

adapt.title: Re-Calibration on Benign Flows from the Target Day (Zero-Day Recall / Benign FPR, Mean over 5 Seeds)
adapt.notes: Warm-up windows are the earliest W benign flows of the target day and are excluded from evaluation; the oracle re-calibrates on 2,000 benign flows sampled at random from the day. recal+ref also adds one third of the window to the k-NN reference; methods without a k-NN component change only through the smaller calibration split.

gate.title: Deployed Zero-Day Gate vs. the Frozen v1.1 Detector on Flows Neither Model Trained On
gate.notes: Flows in both models' test splits and in neither model's training or validation data (39,221 benign, 15,177 known attacks, 47 never-seen). Per-family recall at α = 1%, gate vs. v1.1 (n): Bot 0.927 vs. 0.585 (n = 82); BruteForce 1.000 vs. 0.995 (n = 370); DDoS 1.000 vs. 1.000 (n = 5,089); DoS 0.999 vs. 0.995 (n = 5,955); PortScan 1.000 vs. 1.000 (n = 3,604); WebAttack 1.000 vs. 0.416 (n = 77). Bot and WebAttack have fewer than 100 eligible flows; treat their rates as indicative.

v11_2018.title: Frozen v1.1 Detector Scored Unchanged on CSE-CIC-IDS2018
v11_2018.notes: CSE-CIC-IDS2018 sample v2: up to 20,000 flows per attack label and 200,000 benign flows from 10 capture days; labels mapped to CICIDS2017 families; features mapped to the 2017 schema. Nothing was retrained or re-thresholded. IID CICIDS2017 test F1 for reference: 0.990.

cross.title: Open-Set Detection Trained on CICIDS2017, Tested on CSE-CIC-IDS2018 (α = 1%, Mean over 5 Seeds, Sample v2)
cross.notes: Unknown family: Infiltration (never in CICIDS2017 training). No CSE-CIC-IDS2018 data was used for training; recalibration results per capture day are in the next table.

cross_perday.title: CSE-CIC-IDS2018 per Capture Day: Aegis-OSR before and after Same-Day Re-Calibration (α = 1%)
cross_perday.notes: Trained once on CICIDS2017 per seed. For each 2018 day independently the warm-up window is that day's earliest benign flows; evaluation uses only the rest of that day (no overlap). Recall is attack recall on the day's attacks (Infiltration days: zero-day recall). Re-calibration cells: recall / benign FPR. '—' = no benign flows left for that window size. On 2018-02-21 the flows labelled benign have a median of 842,917 bytes/s against 1,129 on the other days, consistent with documented labelling problems in CSE-CIC-IDS2018; the day is reported as is.

families.title: 10 Classifier Families at a 1% Benign False-Alarm Budget: Seen vs. Withheld Families (Seed 1)
families.notes: Single seed, no confidence intervals. Thresholds set on validation benign flows for a 1% false-alarm rate. 'Hist. gradient boosting' is scikit-learn's LightGBM-style implementation; the CNN and LSTM read the 77 features as a 1-D sequence (no time axis).

range_def.title: Cyber Range: Defense Comparison
range_def.notes: Mean over 9 scenarios, 10 seeds each, automatic response. Means hide that most scenarios are cheap for the server; with monitoring only, availability during the attack averaged 66% (DOS; worst second 37%) and 41% (DDOS; worst second 25%). Availability is modelled (capacity / load), not measured on a real service; isolation is lifted 5 s after the attack stops, so its recovery time reflects scenario length. '—' = not applicable.

range_det.title: Cyber Range: Which Detector Raises the Incident
range_det.notes: 10 seeds per cell; incident rule 3 alerts within 5 s. Shown: scenarios where a detector missed runs or had attack-flow recall below 0.99. The other 6 scenarios were detected by both detectors in every run (mean latency 0.0–2.4 s). Mean false incidents per run across all cells: 0.01. The zero-day scenario redraws the same 47 never-seen flows, so its runs are not independent zero-days.

xai.title: Explanation Stability of the Frozen Detector (20 Flows per Class, Seed 7)
xai.notes: Consistency, robustness and agreement are mean Jaccard overlaps of top-five SHAP features (1 = identical); bold marks robustness below 0.90. Rank stability is the Spearman correlation of the top-ten attribution magnitudes with and without noise. Flows come from the leakage-free replay pool (neither model trained on them).

p11.title: Mitigation Measured on the Controlled Test Plane (10 Repetitions, Frozen-ML Detection)
p11.notes: Measured effectiveness on the CONTROLLED test adapter (no live firewall). Δ = measured − assumed storyboard prior.
